title: Participant first-password claim still trusts knowledge of the registered email address

original_titles.title: First-login password claim enables account pre-claim takeover
First-login password claim enables takeover of unactivated accounts
First-login account claiming bypasses invite activation (ATH-02a/02b S2, documented deviation)
First-login claim flow: NULL password_hash accounts are claimable and disqualified accounts get re-activated
Login accepts any typed password for accounts with an empty password_hash (bootstrap takeover path)
Login page copy contradicts itself about account creation; first-sign-in password capture lacks strength meter

problem: PR #59 prevents staff accounts from claiming passwords and requires a participant to have a team membership before claiming. However, any person who knows a registered participant email and reaches the login page before the participant can choose the initial password. Mailbox ownership is explicitly not verified.
impact: A participant account can still be pre-claimed, allowing impersonation, false reports and consumption of submission caps. This is an accepted event policy in the current UI/docs, not a fully solved authentication problem.

evidence_paths: backend/app/routers/auth.py: login branch for role == participant and password_hash is NULL
verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Choose and document one policy before the next event: (A) verified email OTP, (B) one-time organizer-generated claim secret delivered in person, or (C) admin-assigned participant passwords with forced change at first login. Do not silently combine these methods.
For the preferred one-time claim method, store only a hash of a random 128-bit token, bind it to user_id + event_id, expiry and one-time use, and rate-limit attempts per account and IP.
Require the token plus password creation before issuing a normal session. A participant with password_hash NULL must always receive generic AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS unless the claim proof is valid.
Record claim issuance, delivery method, claim success/failure and revocation in the audit log without logging the raw secret.
Add tests for pre-claim attacker, expired token, replay, wrong account, wrong event, brute-force rate limiting and a successful legitimate claim.

acceptance_criteria: A person who only knows the email cannot claim the account.
Claim secrets are single-use, short-lived, hashed at rest and never logged.
Unknown accounts and invalid claims have indistinguishable outward credential errors.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.

residual_risk_or_scope_note: If the event owner intentionally retains email-only first claim, this remains an accepted risk and must be presented as such. The current requirement to distribute emails through a controlled channel is not cryptographic proof of mailbox ownership.
